decides: Weak confirmation only. Per rated watt, ACOPOWER's 120W PLK ($2.17/W, 8.6 W/lb) beats the 100W Renogy N-Type suitcase ($2.30/W) at today's store prices. Without the Renogy suitcase's Imp and weight from an opened page, I can't compute battery-side watts per dollar, and that figure is what would decide between the PWM kits. ChatGPT's 200W Renogy pick ($322.99 on its card) could not be re-priced per variant today because storecheck reports only the listing's minimum variant ($229.99, compare-at $322.99).

findings.label: Why PWM nameplate watts overstate battery-side watts (worked example on a Renogy 200W panel)
findings.value: about 132 W into a 13.3 V battery from a 200 W panel through PWM
findings.source_title: E.Flex 100/200W N-Type Portable Solar Panel | Renogy US
findings.note: A PWM controller pulls the panel down to battery voltage, so output ≈ Imp × Vbatt. Renogy lists the E.Flex 200W at Imp 9.92 A and Vmp 20.16 V. 9.92 A × 13.3 V (illustrative LiFePO4 resting voltage, not sourced) = 132 W, about 66% of 200 W. Illustrative only: the E.Flex has no built-in controller and is not a candidate.
